operators.name: embedding_add_forward

parameters.name: x1
parameters.layout: contiguous or strided; indices are read as int64

parameters.name: x2
parameters.layout: contiguous or strided; indices are read as int64

parameters.name: weight1
parameters.layout: contiguous or strided; rows are embedding vectors

parameters.name: weight2
parameters.layout: contiguous or strided; rows are embedding vectors

semantics: For each pair of indices (x1[b,s], x2[b,s]), loads the corresponding row from weight1 and weight2 respectively and adds them element-wise.
Indices outside [0, num_embeddings_1-1] or [0, num_embeddings_2-1] are invalid; behavior is undefined (reference nn.Embedding would raise for out-of-range indices, so inputs are assumed in range).
The output tensor has shape [batch, seq_len, embedding_dim], matching the shape of each embedding lookup, and is float32 on the current CUDA device.
The two embedding lookups are performed independently (no cross-fusion); the addition is elementwise over the last dimension.
No bias is involved; nn.Embedding has no bias.
Broadcasting is not needed because both lookups and the addition share identical shapes.
The operation must preserve the output order of the flattened batch*seq_len rows.
self.embedding1(x1) returns a float32 CUDA tensor of shape [2048, 512, 64] by gathering rows from embedding1.weight based on x1.
self.embedding2(x2) returns a float32 CUDA tensor of shape [2048, 512, 64] by gathering rows from embedding2.weight based on x2.
The addition is elementwise over all dimensions, producing a float32 CUDA tensor of the same shape.
The final return value is this float32 CUDA tensor with stride [32768, 64, 1] (contiguous).
